title: Throughput Guardrails: Contract Playbook for Dedicated Capacity Guarantees
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: define a pragmatic, customer-readable playbook for Dedicated throughput guarantees that ties SLA definitions to an error-budget construct, explicit autoscale and fleet controls, and a tiered credit remediation model. This ticket produces contract text snippets, an operational escalation flow, measurable SLO definitions, and an implementation checklist for Runtime/Infra/Economics teams.

Context: customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput commitments while retaining flexible autoscale controls. Several recent pilots highlighted disagreement about what constitutes a breach (short spikes vs. sustained underprovision) and how autoscale behavior affects crediting. This doc reconciles product goals (clear entitlements), engineering realities (bursty workloads + autoscale cooldowns), and legal simplicity (contract language easy to audit).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single-source playbook (.confluence link referenced below) that legal can drop into MSAs; 2) Concrete SLO definitions bounded by time-windows (1m, 5m, 1h) and measurable via existing runtime metrics; 3) Error budget computation method with worked examples; 4) Tiered credit table with examples for sustained vs. transient degradations; 5) Implementation notes for autoscale policy interaction and recommended default fleet controls; 6) Sign-off from Legal, Runtime, and GTM leads.
implementation_notes:
SLOs should be evaluated from the customer's reservation viewpoint: 'effective throughput' = tokens successfully served within customer's throughput window / tokens requested given backpressure. Define breach when effective throughput < committed throughput for >= X% of a rolling 1-hour window. Use existing per-customer telemetry (route-level token counters, throttling events, autoscale actions). Runtime team to ensure events are tagged with provisioned_capacity_id and autoscale_event_id for auditability.

Autoscale interplay: recommend a default 'grace window' of 180s during which temporary autoscale activity or cold-start stalls do not count as breaches. Provide an option for customers to opt into a stricter immediate-counting mode for higher credits. Engineers: implement a two-tier measurement stream — fast-window (1m/5m) used for alerting, long-window (1h/24h) used for crediting calculation.

Billing/crediting: credit calculations should be capped monthly and expressed as a percent-of-monthly-fee, with a staircase that differentiates short transient incidents (<5m) vs. sustained incidents (>30m).
contract_language_snippet:
Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Dedicated Throughput capacity available to Customer in accordance with the committed throughput stated in the Order Form. 'Committed Throughput' is measured as the average tokens per second successfully served to Customer's traffic over a rolling one-hour interval.

Remediation & Credits: If Redwood fails to meet the Committed Throughput for a given billing period, Customer will be eligible for service credits computed as follows: (1) For transient degradations (root-cause-categorized as transient autoscale activity or network flapping and lasting <5 minutes): no credit by default; (2) For short sustained degradations (>=5 minutes and <30 minutes within a 24-hour window): credit = 5% of proportional hourly reserved fee per incident; (3) For prolonged degradations (>=30 minutes within a 24-hour window): credit escalates linearly up to 50% of proportional hourly reserved fee depending on duration and recurrence. Credits are capped at 100% of monthly reserved fee. Customer must request credits within 30 days of incident notice.

Exceptions: Credits will not apply where degradation is caused by Customer-configured throttles, rate-limiting rules, or traffic patterns outside documented capacity expectations.
tests_and_monitoring:
Monitoring: implement two dashboards: 'Dedicated Throughput Health (fast)' (1m/5m latency and throughput percent of committed) and 'Dedicated Throughput Billing View (long)' (1h/24h effective throughput vs committed, incident timeline).

Automated Tests: stress tests that simulate bursty traffic and measure effective throughput under autoscale policies; chaos tests that simulate loss of a fraction of GPU pool; regression suite to validate credit computation.

Alerting: severity P0 alert when effective throughput < 90% of committed for 5 continuous minutes; P1 when < 95% for 10 minutes. Triage playbook link included.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilots, 2 weeks): run credit computation on historical pilot data and validate results with Finance. Phase 2 (select customers, 4 weeks): opt-in for beta customers with explicit support engagement and run live telemetry + manual credits. Phase 3 (general availability, 2 weeks): add to order forms and automate credit issuance and PRs to billing. Communicate via customer newsletter and a KB article.
review_feedback:
- Legal (R. Singh): prefer clearer definition of 'rolling one-hour interval' and timeline for credit request; asked to shorten claim window to 15 days.
- Runtime (A. Alvarez): recommended increasing grace window to 180s and adding explicit tagging of autoscale events to telemetry.
- Finance (S. Patel): requested upper cap on credits at monthly reserved fee and example computations to avoid revenue volatility.
- Support (K. Johnson): asked for a non-technical summary for CSMs and a template email for incident communication.
open_questions:
1) Should we allow customers to choose between 'immediate counting' vs 'grace window' modes in the contract? Tradeoff: more customer choice increases complexity in billing automation.
2) How to categorize root causes for credit eligibility (runtime bug, infra cloud outage, customer misconfig)? Need an incident taxonomy owned by SRE.
3) Do we provide retroactive credits for incidents before GA if detected later? Legal prefers a clear cutoff.
4) Minimum signal thresholds for small customers — avoid false positives when committed throughput is low.
next_steps:
1) Incorporate Legal feedback and finalize contract snippet (owner: Maya). 2) Runtime to add autoscale_event_id tagging and implement measurement streams (owner: Ajay Rao). 3) Finance to model credit scenarios and approve caps (owner: S. Patel). 4) Prepare KB + CSM email template (owner: K. Johnson). 5) Schedule cross-functional review for 2026-03-20.
